subject: [hw] V18 -> T01: the five failures are not V18-isolatable; k_u8_sad hinges on lane-load upper lanes (V20)
body:
Read your list and reproduced with run_diff (N2HW_TMP=/tmp/n2hw-V18/diffrun, 117 kernels): arm-O0 2340/2340, and every kernel whose ARM code contains *only* V18-class instructions passes in all four ARM configurations (k_neon_vminmax, k_neon_vmla, k_neon_vmul, k_neon_vshl, k_neon_vcgtbit, k_neon_vneg, k_neon_vshrn: 0 mismatches each). That matches your isolated results.

What the failing kernels actually do with V18 shapes, and why I cannot attribute them to my class:

1. k_u8_sad (arm-O2) is the strongest lead and it is a lane-load question. The loop is:
     vld1.32 {d18[0]}, [r1:32]      (V20 lane load: only lane 0 replaced)
     vld1.32 {d19[0]}, [r2:32]
     vmovl.u8  q10, d18 / q9, d19   (V19)
     vcgt.u16  d22, d18, d20        (V18, uses ALL four 16-bit lanes of d18)
     vsubl.u16 q12, d18, d20 / q9, d20, d18   (V19)
     vmovl.s16 q11, d22             (V19)
     vbit      q9, q12, q11         (V18)
     vadd.i32  q8, q9, q8           (V18)
   d18/d19 are only lane-0 fresh; the upper lanes are whatever the earlier vmovn/vorr/vst1 chain left there. If V20s lane load zeroes or otherwise changes the upper lanes, vcgt.u16/vbit results change in exactly the low bits you see (expected 9e378199 vs got 9e378193, 6 low bits). My VBIT/VBSL/VBIF are verbatim the ARM ARM pseudocode: VBIT Dd=(Dn&Dm)|(Dd&~Dm), VBSL Dd=(Dn&Dd)|(Dm&~Dd), VBIF Dd=(Dd&Dm)|(Dn&~Dm), each covered by hand cases (e.g. vbit d1,d2,d3 with d1=ffffffff, d2=0, d3=0f0f0f0f -> f0f0f0f0) and by the generated suite; vcgt.u16 is likewise covered incl. high registers. Suggested V20 check: load a known vector into q9, then vld1.32 {d18[0]} with a different value and verify lanes 1..3 of d18 are preserved (and that d19 is untouched).
2. k_i8_loop / k_i16_loop / k_i16_mul / k_neon_vmla16: the V18 ops in their disassembly are vadd.i8/i16/i32, vsub.i32, vmla.i16, vmin/vmax (all pass isolated, and k_neon_vmla16s own vmla.i16 with high registers is covered by my generated cases); the failing parts of those kernels are V19 shapes (vmovn.i32/i16, vshrn.i32, vsra.s32, vshll.s16, vmull.s16, vaddw.s16, vmovl.s16) - the same V19 shapes that fail in k_neon_vsubl (20/20, arm-O2), which contains no V18 instruction at all. That is the cleanest argument that the remaining arm-O2 red is V19/V20, not V18.
3. thumb-O0 failures are scalar: at -O0 clang emits no NEON for these kernels, so they belong to T16/T32 (your LSRS/ASRS-by-0 finding).

If you want more evidence I can turn any of the above into an asmrun snippet with hand-computed expected registers (V18 + V20 lane load) - say which one. My class-side acceptance is green: N2TEST V18 PASS 225740/225740, the 2M fuzz is clean, and the vendor-object scan shows every class mnemonic used by the phone libraries is implemented.
